```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r}
library(z3r)
ctx <- z3_context()
x <- z3_int(ctx, "x")
y <- z3_int(ctx, "y")
```

`z3_optimize()` is a solver that also minimizes or maximizes objectives and
satisfies as many weighted soft constraints as it can. It finds global
optima of linear integer and real problems, MaxSAT problems, and
combinations with any other theory.

## Objectives

```{r}
opt <- z3_optimize(ctx)
z3_add(opt, x >= 0, y >= 0, x + 2 * y <= 14, 3 * x - y >= 0, x - y <= 2)
profit <- z3_maximize(opt, 3 * x + 4 * y)
z3_check(opt)
z3_optimum(profit)
z3_model_values(z3_model(opt))
```

## When the optimum is not a number

An objective may be unbounded, or have a bound it never reaches. z3r says so
instead of returning a misleading number:

```{r}
r <- z3_real(ctx, "r")
o1 <- z3_optimize(ctx)
z3_add(o1, x >= 0)
h1 <- z3_maximize(o1, x)
z3_check(o1)
z3_optimum(h1)

o2 <- z3_optimize(ctx)
z3_add(o2, r < 3)
h2 <- z3_maximize(o2, r)
z3_check(o2)
z3_optimum(h2)
```

The second optimum is a supremum: `r` can approach 3 but never equal it. Z3
writes it as `3 - epsilon`.

## Several objectives

By default objectives are lexicographic: the first is optimized first.

```{r}
lex <- z3_optimize(ctx)
z3_add(lex, x + y <= 10, x >= 0, y >= 0, x <= 7, y <= 7)
hx <- z3_maximize(lex, x)
hy <- z3_maximize(lex, y)
z3_check(lex)
c(x = z3_value(z3_optimum(hx)$value), y = z3_value(z3_optimum(hy)$value))
```

`priority = "box"` optimizes each objective on its own, and `"pareto"`
enumerates Pareto-optimal points, one per call to `z3_check()`:

```{r}
box <- z3_optimize(ctx, priority = "box")
z3_add(box, x + y <= 10, x >= 0, y >= 0, x <= 7, y <= 7)
bx <- z3_maximize(box, x)
by <- z3_maximize(box, y)
z3_check(box)
c(x = z3_value(z3_optimum(bx)$value), y = z3_value(z3_optimum(by)$value))
```

## Soft constraints (MaxSAT)

Soft constraints are preferences with weights; the optimizer minimizes the
total weight it has to give up. Groups of soft constraints (`id`) act as
separate objectives.

```{r}
staff <- z3_bools(ctx, c("ana", "ben", "cai", "dee"))
opt <- z3_optimize(ctx)
# At least two people on shift, Ana and Ben are never on together
z3_add(opt, z3_atleast(staff, k = 2), !(staff$ana & staff$ben))
z3_add_soft(opt, !staff$ana, 3)   # Ana prefers to be off
z3_add_soft(opt, !staff$cai, 1)
z3_add_soft(opt, !staff$dee, 2)
z3_add_soft(opt, staff$ben, 1)
z3_check(opt)
unlist(z3_model_values(z3_model(opt)))
```

## Scheduling with disjunctions

Disjunctive constraints make the feasible region non-convex; this is where
SMT-based optimization is at home.

```{r}
dur <- c(4, 3, 2, 5)
start <- z3_ints(ctx, paste0("s", 1:4))
opt <- z3_optimize(ctx)
for (i in 1:4) z3_add(opt, start[[i]] >= 0)
for (i in 1:3) for (j in (i + 1):4) {
  z3_add(opt, start[[i]] + dur[i] <= start[[j]] | start[[j]] + dur[j] <= start[[i]])
}
z3_add(opt, start$s2 + dur[2] <= start$s4)       # job 2 before job 4
end <- z3_int(ctx, "end")
for (i in 1:4) z3_add(opt, end >= start[[i]] + dur[i])
z3_add_soft(opt, start$s1 == 0, 2)                # prefer job 1 first
mk <- z3_minimize(opt, end)
z3_check(opt)
z3_optimum(mk)
unlist(z3_model_values(z3_model(opt))[paste0("s", 1:4)])
```

## Watching progress

`z3_on_model()` calls an R function with every improved model, which is
useful for long optimizations:

```{r}
opt <- z3_optimize(ctx)
z3_add(opt, x >= 0, x <= 1000, x %% 7 == 3)
z3_maximize(opt, x)
seen <- c()
z3_on_model(opt, function(m) seen <<- c(seen, z3_value(z3_eval(m, x))))
z3_check(opt)
seen
```

## Limits

* Over nonlinear arithmetic, quantifiers and some other theories the
  optimizer may return `"unknown"` or an answer that is not optimal.
* An optimizer interrupted by Ctrl-C, a timeout or `rlimit` returns
  `"unknown"` with reason `"canceled"`; Z3 does not distinguish them.
* Optimizers do not support tactics or unsat-core minimization.
